overview: This Senate resolution recognizes polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) as a serious health condition and supports naming September 2026 "PCOS Awareness Month." PCOS is a common hormonal and metabolic disorder in women and girls that can cause irregular periods, infertility and other symptoms, and is linked to higher risks of diabetes, heart disease, some cancers and mental health problems. The resolution notes that researchers estimate about 10 percent of U.S. women have it, that many cases go undiagnosed, that there is no known cure, and that a new name, polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), was chosen in 2026. It calls for more research, better diagnosis and treatment, and encourages states and localities to support awareness efforts. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 30, 2026.
for: Supporters say greater awareness could lead to earlier diagnosis of a common but often missed condition and encourage more research into its causes and treatment.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it does not change any law or provide new funding for research.
